import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Handle NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' by filling them with 'No Disorder'
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Set a clean and professional seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8)) # Adjust figure size for better readability
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    size='Stress Level', # Use Stress Level to vary point size, adding another dimension
    sizes=(50, 400), # Range for point sizes
    alpha=0.7, # Transparency to help with overplotting
    edgecolor='w', # White edge for points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5 # Line width for the edge
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Sleep Disorder and Stress Level', fontsize=18, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (Hours)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 Scale)', fontsize=14)

# Customize the legend
# Place the legend outside the plot area to avoid obscuring data
plt.legend(title='Sleep Disorder', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0, fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

# Improve layout to prevent labels/legend from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Handle NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' by filling them with 'No Disorder'
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Set a clean and professional seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8)) # Adjust figure size for better readability
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    size='Stress Level', # Use Stress Level to vary point size, adding another dimension
    sizes=(50, 400), # Range for point sizes
    alpha=0.7, # Transparency to help with overplotting
    edgecolor='w', # White edge for points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5 # Line width for the edge
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Sleep Disorder and Stress Level', fontsize=18, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (Hours)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 Scale)', fontsize=14)

# Customize the legend
# Place the legend outside the plot area to avoid obscuring data
plt.legend(title='Sleep Disorder', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0, fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

# Improve layout to prevent labels/legend from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend
